Define Artificial Intelligence and describe Intelligent Agents. Formulate the PEAS (Performance measure, Environment, Actuators, Sensors) description and agent environment characteristics for an Automated Autonomous Taxi Driver.
questions.solutionOutline: Agent perceives environment via sensors and acts upon environment via actuators. Taxi PEAS: Performance (safety, speed, passenger comfort, legal compliance, profit); Environment (roads, traffic, pedestrians, weather); Actuators (steering, accelerator, brake, horn, display); Sensors (cameras, LiDAR, radar, GPS, speedometer, odometer). Environment is partially observable, stochastic, sequential, dynamic, continuous, and multi-agent.

questions.text: Compare Uninformed Search Strategies: Breadth First Search (BFS), Depth First Search (DFS), Uniform Cost Search (UCS), and Iterative Deepening Search (IDS) in terms of completeness, time complexity, space complexity, and optimality.
questions.solutionOutline: BFS: complete, optimal for uniform step cost, time O(b^d), space O(b^d) (memory bound). DFS: incomplete in infinite trees, not optimal, time O(b^m), space O(bm) (space efficient). UCS: complete, optimal for any positive step costs, time and space O(b^(1 + floor(C*/epsilon))). IDS: combines completeness and optimality of BFS with linear space complexity O(bd) of DFS.

questions.text: Explain Hill Climbing Search and discuss local extrema problems: Local Maxima, Plateaus, and Ridges. How does Simulated Annealing search escape local optima using the Metropolis probability criterion $P = e^{-\Delta E / T}$?
questions.solutionOutline: Greedy local search moving continuously in direction of increasing elevation. Failures: Local maximum (higher than neighbors but sub-optimal globally), Plateau (flat area where evaluation function is constant), Ridge (steep sides sloping up gently along crest). Simulated Annealing allows downhill moves with probability P = exp(-Delta E / T); high temperature T allows exploration, while cooling T -> 0 converges to global optimum.

questions.text: Explain First-Order Predicate Logic (FOPL) resolution refutation. Convert given English statements into FOPL, convert to Conjunctive Normal Form (CNF / Clausal Form), and prove a theorem using resolution and unification algorithm with substitution $\theta$.
questions.solutionOutline: Steps to CNF: 1) Eliminate implications; 2) Move negations inward (De Morgan); 3) Standardize variables; 4) Skolemization (replace existential quantifiers with Skolem constants/functions); 5) Drop universal quantifiers; 6) Distribute OR over AND. Negate the goal clause, resolve complementary literals through Most General Unifier (MGU), deriving empty clause (contradiction) to prove theorem.

questions.text: Explain Semantic Networks, Frames, and Conceptual Dependencies for structured knowledge representation. Illustrate inheritance hierarchies and default reasoning using suitable domain examples.
questions.solutionOutline: Semantic Networks represent knowledge as graph: nodes represent objects/concepts, directed edges represent relationships (IS-A, HAS-A). Frames organize knowledge into prototype data structures with named slots and default facet values, supporting inheritance. Conceptual Dependencies (Schank) decompose natural language actions into primitive acts (ATRANS, PTRANS, MTRANS, PROPEL, INGEST) independent of surface syntax.

questions.text: Describe the architecture of an Expert System. Explain Knowledge Acquisition, Inference Engine (Forward Chaining vs Backward Chaining), Rule-Based System, and Conflict Resolution strategies.
questions.solutionOutline: Architecture: Knowledge Base (rules/facts), Inference Engine, Working Memory, User Interface, Explanation Facility. Forward chaining is data-driven (starts with known facts and fires rules to deduce conclusions; used in monitoring/synthesis). Backward chaining is goal-driven (starts with hypothesis and checks if facts support premises; used in medical diagnosis). Conflict resolution: specificity, recency, priority.

questions.text: Explain Fuzzy Logic and Fuzzy Sets. Contrast crisp sets with fuzzy membership functions $\mu_A(x) \in [0, 1]$. Detail the four steps of a Fuzzy Inference System (Mamdani Model): Fuzzification, Rule Evaluation, Aggregation, and Defuzzification (Centroid Method).
questions.solutionOutline: Crisp set has binary membership {0, 1}; fuzzy set allows continuous degree of truth [0, 1] representing vagueness. Mamdani steps: 1) Fuzzification: map crisp input to fuzzy linguistic values (Low, Med, High); 2) Rule evaluation: compute firing strength using min (AND) or max (OR); 3) Aggregation: combine outputs of active rules using max; 4) Defuzzification: compute crisp output using center of gravity z* = sum(mu(z)*z) / sum(mu(z)).

questions.text: Describe the workflow of Genetic Algorithms (GA). Explain Chromosome Encoding, Fitness Function evaluation, Selection mechanisms (Roulette Wheel, Tournament), Crossover operators (Single-point, Two-point), and Mutation probability.
questions.solutionOutline: Stochastic search based on Darwinian natural selection. Workflow: Initialize population of candidate chromosomes -> Evaluate fitness -> Selection (Roulette wheel assigns probability p_i = f_i / sum(f_j)) -> Crossover (recombines genetic material of parents at random cut-points with probability p_c ~ 0.8) -> Mutation (flips random bits with low probability p_m ~ 0.01 to maintain genetic diversity) -> Terminate on convergence.

questions.text: Explain Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) and derive the Backpropagation Algorithm. Compute weight update formulas using gradient descent $\Delta w = -\eta \frac{\partial E}{\partial w}$ with Sigmoid activation function.
questions.solutionOutline: Feedforward neural net with input, hidden, and output layers. Forward pass computes net activations and outputs: y = sigma(z). Error E = 0.5 sum (t_k - y_k)^2. Output layer error gradient delta_k = (t_k - y_k) * y_k * (1 - y_k). Hidden layer gradient delta_j = y_j * (1 - y_j) * sum (delta_k * w_jk). Weight updates: Delta w_jk = eta * delta_k * y_j; Delta w_ij = eta * delta_j * x_i.

questions.text: What is Reinforcement Learning? Describe the Agent-Environment interaction loop, Markov Decision Process (MDP: $S, A, P, R, \gamma$), the Bellman Equation, and the Q-Learning value iteration update algorithm.
questions.solutionOutline: Agent learns optimal policy through trial-and-error reward signals. MDP defined by states S, actions A, transition probability P(s'|s,a), reward R(s,a), discount factor gamma. Bellman optimality equation: V*(s) = max_a [R(s,a) + gamma sum P(s'|s,a) V*(s')]. Q-Learning is model-free TD control: Q(s, a) <- Q(s, a) + alpha [r + gamma max_{a'} Q(s', a') - Q(s, a)].

questions.text: Explain Natural Language Processing (NLP) pipeline phases: Morphological analysis, Syntactic parsing (Context-Free Grammars), Semantic analysis, and Pragmatic/Discourse processing. Discuss ambiguity challenges.
questions.solutionOutline: NLP pipeline: 1) Morphology: analyze word forms, stems, affixes; 2) Syntax: parse sentence structure into parse trees using CFGs and CYK/Earley parsers; 3) Semantics: derive literal meaning from word meanings (lexical semantics, WordNet); 4) Pragmatics: interpret meaning in context and real-world intent. Ambiguities: lexical (polysemy), syntactic (attachment ambiguity), semantic (scope ambiguity).

questions.text: Explain Edge Detection and Feature Extraction in Machine Vision. Describe the Sobel operator, Prewitt operator, and the multi-stage Canny Edge Detection algorithm (Gaussian smoothing, Gradient magnitude/direction, Non-maximum suppression, Hysteresis thresholding).
questions.solutionOutline: Edges mark intensity discontinuities corresponding to physical object boundaries. Sobel applies 3x3 convolution kernels G_x and G_y computing spatial gradient magnitude sqrt(G_x^2 + G_y^2). Canny: 1) Gaussian filter suppresses noise; 2) Computes gradient magnitude and direction; 3) Non-maximum suppression thins edges to 1-pixel width; 4) Double hysteresis thresholding (T_high, T_low) suppresses weak isolated noise edges.

questions.text: Explain Constraint Satisfaction Problems (CSP). Formalize the 8-Queens Problem or Map Coloring Problem as a CSP and explain Backtracking search with Forward Checking and the Arc Consistency (AC-3) algorithm.
questions.solutionOutline: CSP defined by Variables X, Domains D, Constraints C. Map coloring: variables = territories, domain = {Red, Green, Blue}, constraints = neighboring territories cannot have identical colors. Backtracking assigns one variable at a time. Forward checking removes incompatible values from neighboring domains. AC-3 maintains directed arcs (Xi, Xj) in queue, pruning domain values having no support, detecting failure early.

questions.text: Explain Bayesian Networks (Belief Networks) and probabilistic reasoning under uncertainty. Given a Conditional Probability Table (CPT) network, compute joint probabilities and posterior beliefs using Bayes' Rule.
questions.solutionOutline: DAG representing conditional dependencies among random variables. Nodes are variables, directed edges represent conditional influences. Joint probability distribution: P(X_1, ..., X_n) = prod_{i=1}^n P(X_i | Parents(X_i)). Allows computing diagnostic, causal, and intercausal (explaining away) inferences using Bayes rule P(Cause|Effect) = P(Effect|Cause)*P(Cause) / P(Effect).
